unit.why: A brief anecdote, told by the Ropshitzer, about R. Haikel of Amdur: his asceticism and study brought him no rest until he came to the Maggid of Mezritch. It is embedded in a homiletic passage on the need to cleave to the tzaddikim.
unit.boundary_note: part of a continuous homiletic discourse on cleaving to tzaddikim that runs from the previous division into the next; the narrative core is only the first sentence

stories.start_quote: כאשר נשמע מה״ק של הה״ק מראויץ
stories.summary_en: The Rebbe of Ropshitz told that R. Haikel of Amdur found no peace for his soul despite great self-mortification and sleepless study, until he came to the Maggid of Mezritch, where his tikkun was completed. The author uses this to argue that one must join the tzaddikim of the Besht's light.
